title: Slices Pinned to a Given Min and Max
statement:
You get an integer array nums and two integers lo and hi. Count the contiguous, non-empty slices of nums whose smallest value is exactly lo and whose largest value is exactly hi.

The count can be larger than 2³¹, so return it as a full-size integer.

examples.why: [2, 4], [2, 4, 3], [2, 4, 3, 2] and [4, 3, 2]. No valid slice can include the 6, and [4, 3] is missing a 2.
When lo equals hi, one element plays both roles, so all 6 slices count.
The 1s are below lo and act as walls. Inside [5, 2, 5], the slices holding the 2 and a 5 are [5, 2], [2, 5] and [5, 2, 5].

hints: Any value below lo or above hi can never be inside a valid slice. What does that do to the array?
Fix the right end of the slice at index i. A start works if it is after the last out-of-range value and no later than both the last lo and the last hi seen so far.
Track three indexes while scanning: the last bad value, the last lo, the last hi. At each i add max(0, min(lastLo, lastHi) − lastBad).

explain.intuition:
Values outside [lo, hi] are walls: no valid slice can contain one. Between walls, a slice is valid as soon as it contains at least one lo and at least one hi.

Count slices by their right end i. Going left from i, a start s works when the slice [s, i] reaches back to cover the most recent lo and the most recent hi, so s ≤ min(lastLo, lastHi), and it must not cross the most recent wall, so s > lastBad. That gives min(lastLo, lastHi) − lastBad choices, or zero if negative. One pass, three numbers.
steps: For each index i: if nums[i] < lo or nums[i] > hi, set lastBad = i.
If nums[i] === lo, set lastLo = i. If nums[i] === hi, set lastHi = i. Check both, since they can be equal.
pitfalls: Using else if for the lo and hi checks. When lo === hi one element must update both.
Not clamping at zero. If the last lo or hi is behind the last wall, the difference is negative and must add nothing.
Storing the answer in a 32-bit integer: 100 000 equal values give about 5 · 10⁹ slices.

solutions.title: Every start, extend to the right
solutions.idea: For each start, extend the slice while tracking its min and max, and stop at the first wall.

solutions.title: Last wall, last lo, last hi
solutions.idea: For each right end, the valid starts are those after the last wall and no later than the last lo and the last hi.

followups: Count slices whose min is at least lo and whose max is at most hi, without requiring them to be hit exactly. How does the formula simplify?
Answer many (lo, hi) queries on the same array. What would you precompute?
